adoration: Before you ask for anything, tell God one thing you love about who he is.
Think of the most beautiful place you’ve ever stood. Praise the one who made it.
God never gets tired of you. Take a moment to simply praise him for that.
Name three words that describe God. Pray each one back to him slowly.
Look out the nearest window. Praise God for something he made that you can see.
God was here long before your phone and will be here long after. Rest in how big that is.
Tell God he’s good, even if today doesn’t feel good yet.
Everything else keeps changing. Praise God for being the same yesterday, today and tomorrow.
Your feed shows you everyone else. For one minute, look only at God and tell him what you see.
Praise God for being near, not distant. He’s closer than the screen in your hand.
God knows every star by name, and he knows yours. Sit with that for a moment and praise him.
Tell God what amazes you about him right now, in your own words. No fancy language needed.
Picture the ocean, the sky, the mountains. Now praise the one who’s bigger than all of it.
Praise God for his kindness. Not the kindness you earned, the kindness he simply is.
Say “God, you are holy” and let that be the whole prayer for a few breaths.
Praise God for being a Father who never scrolls past you.
Think about how creative God is: color, music, laughter. Praise him for his imagination.
God is faithful even when you aren’t. Tell him how much that means to you.
Praise God for his patience. He has never once given up on you.
Whatever is loud today, God is still on his throne. Praise him for that steadiness.
Tell God he’s worthy of your attention, before anything else gets it.
God doesn’t just give love, he is love. Tell him what that means to you today.
Praise God for something in nature that made you stop and stare this week.
Take one slow breath and say, “You are good.” Take another and say, “You are here.”
God isn’t in a hurry. Slow down and praise him at his pace, not your phone’s.
Praise Jesus for coming close, for choosing to live a human life like ours.
God sees everything and still chooses mercy. Worship him for that.
Praise God for his wisdom. He knows what you need before you find the words.
Imagine God smiling at you. Tell him what you love about his heart.
Praise God for being your safe place, steadier than any person or plan.
God made you able to laugh, taste and wonder. Praise him for being that generous.
Tell God he is enough. Say it even if part of you is still learning to believe it.
Praise God for being a God who listens. You have his full attention right now.
Worship God for who he is when nobody’s watching and nothing is being posted.
Praise God for his power, then remember how gently he uses it with you.
God paints every sunrise. Praise him for the one he gave you today.
Think of a song that reminds you of God. Hum a line and let it be your praise.
Praise God that he’s not a trend. He was, he is, and he always will be.
God is fully present in this moment. Meet him here with a simple “thank you for being you.”
Tell God one thing about him you want to understand better. Praise him for being that deep.
Praise God for being holy and still welcoming you in, exactly as you are.
God doesn’t need a filter. Praise him for being completely real and completely good.
Name something God has done, in history or in your life. Praise him for who that shows he is.
Praise God for his love that never runs out, never resets, and never needs a refresh.
Tell God you love him, simply, without asking for anything in return.
Think of the smallest creature you’ve seen lately. Praise God for caring about details.
Name one of God’s promises that has held up in your life. Praise him for keeping his word.
Praise God for his justice. He sees every wrong and cares about every person.
Say “You are great” to God slowly, and let a moment of silence follow.
Listen to the sounds around you. Praise God for the world that keeps humming under his care.
Worship Jesus for his humility: the God of everything, kneeling to wash feet.
Hold out your open hands. Tell God how small you feel next to him, and how loved.
Marvel at God’s mercy, which meets you before you even ask for it.
Praise God for being a good shepherd who leads you without pushing.
Which name for God means the most to you today? Say it to him and tell him why.
Admire God the way you’d admire a sunset: no agenda, just wonder.
Delight in God’s joy. He takes pleasure in what he made, and that includes you.
Lift your eyes for a moment and honor God for being higher than every worry.
Worship Jesus for his compassion, the way he stopped for people everyone else ignored.
Consider how God holds every atom together. Praise him for keeping the world running.
Honor the Holy Spirit as your helper, the one who prays for you when words run out.
Speak one sentence of praise for each season of life God has walked through with you.
Tell God he is beautiful. Let yourself mean it, even if it feels new to say.
Praise God for being slow to anger and quick to forgive.
Celebrate God’s goodness out loud, the way you’d brag about someone you love.
Wonder at the fact that God wants to be known. Praise him for showing himself to you.
Bow your head and honor God as King over every screen, every headline and every heart.
Imagine every voice in history that has praised God. Add yours with one sentence now.
confession: Is there anything you’d rather God didn’t see today? Tell him, knowing he already loves you.
Name one moment today when you weren’t the person you want to be. Hand it to God.
Be honest about the scrolling, with no shame. God can work with the truth.
Where did you choose the easy thing over the right thing this week? Tell God plainly.
Ask God to show you one thing that’s been crowding him out lately.
Confess any comparison that’s been stealing your joy. Let God reset your eyes.
Did you say something you regret? Tell God, then ask if there’s someone to make it right with.
Name a worry you’ve been holding instead of trusting. Let it go into God’s hands.
Confession is coming home, not beating yourself up. Tell God what’s been in the way.
Is there a grudge you’ve been feeding? Admit it to God and ask him to soften your heart.
Tell God about the habit you keep promising to quit. He’s not tired of hearing it.
Where have you been pretending lately, with others or with God? Drop the act for a minute.
Admit one way your phone came before people today. Ask God for a better tomorrow.
Bring God the thought you keep replaying that isn’t good for you. He can take it.
Ask God to forgive the impatience you showed someone today, and to grow patience in you.
What have you been running to for comfort instead of God? Name it gently.
Tell God where pride crept in today, then breathe. His grace is bigger than your pride.
Name one thing you did today out of fear instead of love. Ask God for courage next time.
Is there someone you’ve been avoiding? Tell God why, and ask him what to do next.
Confess any jealousy you felt while scrolling. Ask God to help you celebrate others for real.
Tell God about the gap between what you believe and how you lived this week. He meets you in the gap.
Ask God to forgive the unkind thing you thought about someone, even if you never said it.
Name the excuse you’ve been leaning on. Lay it down and ask God for a fresh start.
If you’ve been running from God, stop for one breath. Tell him you’re back.
Confess any lie you’ve told, big or small. Ask God to make you a person of truth.
Admit where you’ve been too hard on yourself. That’s worth bringing to God too.
Tell God about the time you lost today, without beating yourself up. Ask him to redeem tomorrow.
Ask God to show you if there’s anything you need to apologize for. Listen for a moment.
Name what’s been taking up the space that belongs to God. Ask him to take it back.
Bring God the doubts you’ve been hiding. Honest doubt is faith that’s still talking.
Confess any words that hurt someone, online or in person. Ask God to help heal what you broke.
Tell God where you’ve been selfish with your time or money. Ask him for an open hand.
Admit the feeling you scroll to avoid. Invite God into that feeling instead.
Ask God to forgive you for rushing past people today, and to help you really see them tomorrow.
Is there something wrong you’ve stopped calling wrong? Be honest with God, who is gentle with honest people.
Name one place you’ve been ungrateful lately. Ask God for new eyes.
Tell God what you’re ashamed of. You are forgiven, not finished.
Confess where you’ve wanted control more than trust. Open your hands as you pray.
Ask God to search your heart and point out one thing to work on. Just one.
Admit where you’ve chased likes more than love. Ask God what really matters today.
Tell God about a promise you broke. Ask for forgiveness and a way to make it right.
Bring God anything you’ve been hiding from the people who love you. Ask for courage to be known.
Say the hard thing to God, then sit in his kindness for a moment. Confession clears the air.
Ask God to forgive what you can remember and to cover what you can’t.
Confess any gossip you shared or enjoyed hearing. Ask God to guard your words.
Admit where you said yes to something you knew would leave you emptier.
Tell God where you judged someone without knowing their story.
Confess where you’ve taken someone close for granted. Ask God to help you show them love.
Ask God to forgive you for staying silent when you should have spoken up.
Name a moment you made yourself look better at someone else’s expense.
Bring God the anger you’ve been justifying. Ask him what’s underneath it.
Wanting to be right can crowd out kindness. Tell God where that happened lately.
Confess any way you’ve used people to get what you wanted. Ask God for a servant’s heart.
Ask God to forgive the times you kept score in a relationship.
Look back over today. Where did you fall short? Tell God, then receive his mercy.
Own your part in a conflict this week. Tell God without blaming anyone else.
Spiritual pride is sneaky. Confess any moment you felt better than others because of your faith.
Think of something you watched or read that you wish you hadn’t. Ask God for a clean mind.
Admit where you’ve been careless with something God trusted you with.
Have you treated prayer like a vending machine? Tell God you want him, not just his gifts.
Where have you been harsh with someone weaker or younger? Tell God and ask for gentleness.
Confess any bitterness toward God himself. He can hear it, and he stays.
Be honest with God about a motive that wasn’t as pure as it looked.
Recall the help you could have given today and didn’t. Bring it to God without excuses.
Complaining crept in today? Ask God to forgive it and to turn it into gratitude.
Name someone you’ve written off. Ask God to forgive you and help you see them again.
Speak your confession in one simple sentence. Then let God’s forgiveness have the last word.
Admit where you’ve broken a rule you expect everyone else to keep.
thanksgiving: Thank God for one person who made today lighter.
Name three small good things from today. Thank God for each one.
Thank God for something you have right now that you once prayed for.
Thank God for your body and one thing it let you do today.
Think of a meal you enjoyed recently. Thank God for every hand that made it possible.
Thank God for a hard thing that grew you, even if you’d never choose it again.
Thank God for a friend who knows the real you.
Thank God for the roof over your head and the bed you’ll sleep in tonight.
Thank God for a song that has carried you through something.
Thank God for a moment today when you laughed.
Thank God for someone who believed in you before you believed in yourself.
Thank God for something beautiful you saw today that no camera captured.
Thank God for the breath in your lungs. Take a slow one and say thanks.
Thank God for a prayer he answered in a way you didn’t expect.
Thank God for your family, the easy parts and the parts you’re still working on.
Thank God for coffee, sunlight, or whatever small thing got you going this morning.
Thank God for forgiving you. Be specific about something you know he forgave.
Thank God for your work, or for the chance to find work you love.
Thank God for clean water, a warm shower, and the other gifts that are easy to forget.
Thank God for a teacher, coach or mentor who shaped you.
Thank God for a door he closed that you’re now glad stayed shut.
Thank God for one way he has changed you over the past year.
Thank God for the people praying for you, even the ones you don’t know about.
Thank God for a place where you feel at peace.
Thank God for today’s ordinary moments. Ordinary is a gift too.
Thank God that you’re here, praying, instead of scrolling. That’s grace at work.
Thank God for a memory that still makes you smile.
Thank God for the people who walk with you in faith, near or far.
Thank God for something you heard, tasted or smelled today.
Thank God for rest, even if it was just five quiet minutes.
Thank God for someone who forgave you.
Thank God for a skill he gave you, and ask how to use it well.
Thank God for getting you through a day you weren’t sure you’d make it through.
Thank God for the season outside your window right now.
Thank God for Jesus, and for one thing about him that moves you.
Thank God for a kind message someone sent you.
Thank God for the good side of your phone: the people it connects you to.
Thank God for a book, a verse or a sermon that stuck with you.
Thank God for an animal that has brought you joy.
Thank God for this exact moment of quiet.
Thank God for what he’s going to do, even before you see it.
Thank God for a stranger who was kind to you.
Name one person who makes your life fuller, and thank God for them out loud.
Look around the room. Pick one thing and thank God for it like it’s brand new.
Thank God for a door that opened this year that you didn’t even knock on.
Name someone who made you feel seen recently. Thank God for sending them your way.
Think of a time you were protected and only realized it later. Thank God for that.
Say thank you for the people who keep your town running: drivers, cooks, cleaners, repair crews.
Thank God for a worry from last year that never came true.
Look at your last few photos. Pick one moment and thank God for it.
Name a tradition you love, like a holiday meal or a yearly trip. Thank God for it.
Thank God for a piece of advice that changed the way you live.
Tell God about a promise someone kept to you, and thank him for their faithfulness.
Bring to mind a grandparent or elder who shaped you. Thank God for their life.
Thank God for a second chance you were given, and name who gave it to you.
Give thanks for something you learned this week, big or small.
Give God thanks for the patience someone showed you this week.
Remember the friend who checked on you when things were hard. Thank God for them.
Thank God for a need that was met right when you needed it, whether money, food or help.
Recall a doctor, nurse or caregiver who helped you or someone you love. Thank God for them.
Name a child in your life, and thank God for something that delights you about them.
Be thankful for the freedom to pray right now, anywhere, without asking permission.
Think back to a time you got to help someone. Thank God for letting you be part of it.
Tell God thank you for a brother, sister or cousin, and a memory you share with them.
Looking back on a lonely season, thank God for staying when you couldn’t feel him.
Offer thanks for the ability to read, learn and change your mind.
Honor the people who fed you, taught you and raised you. Thank God for each face that comes to mind.
Consider the choices you get to make today. Thank God for the freedom to make them.
supplication: Tell God what you need today in one honest sentence. He wants to hear it.
Ask God for wisdom about the decision you’ve been putting off.
Ask God for strength for the thing you’re dreading this week.
Ask God to help you put your phone down and be present tonight.
Bring God your biggest worry right now. Ask him to carry it with you.
Ask God for peace in the place where you feel the most pressure.
Ask God for rest, the deep kind that sleep alone doesn’t fix.
Ask God to guide your next step, even if you can’t see the whole path.
Ask God to heal what hurts, in your body, your heart, or both.
Ask God to provide for a need you’ve been too proud to mention.
Ask God for courage to have the conversation you’ve been avoiding.
Ask God to help you be kind to the person who’s hardest to be kind to.
Ask God to guard your mind from comparison today.
Ask God for focus on the work in front of you.
Ask God for patience with yourself while you’re still growing.
Ask God to open a door you’ve been praying about, or to give you peace if it stays closed.
Ask God to help you love the people in your home well.
Ask God for a friend who will walk with you in faith.
Ask God to help you break a habit that’s been holding you back.
Ask God to show you how to spend your time in a way you won’t regret.
Ask God to calm your racing thoughts. Breathe slowly while you ask.
Ask God for joy that doesn’t depend on how today goes.
Ask God for a clear head and a soft heart.
Ask God to help you trust him with your future: your work, your relationships, your plans.
Ask God to meet you in your loneliness. Tell him exactly how it feels.
Ask God for self-control with the thing that keeps pulling you in.
Ask God for wisdom with your money this month.
Ask God to protect the people you love today.
Ask God to help you hear his voice above all the noise.
Ask God for faith to believe he’s working, even when it’s quiet.
Ask God to help you forgive someone you’re still angry with.
Ask God for eyes to notice someone who needs help today.
Ask God for good sleep tonight and a fresh start tomorrow.
Ask God for help with something small. Nothing is too small to bring to him.
Ask God to make you brave enough to be honest about how you’re really doing.
Ask God to bring good out of something that went wrong.
Ask God to strengthen your faith where it feels thin right now.
Tell God what you’re hoping for, even the things you’re scared to say out loud.
Ask God to lead you to the right people, and the right people to you.
Ask God for whatever {name} needs most this week.
Bring {name} to God by name and ask him to surround them with peace.
Ask God to give {name} wisdom and strength for what’s in front of them.
Ask God to provide for {name} in a way only he can.
Ask God to heal {name} in body, mind and heart.
Ask God to draw {name} closer to him, gently and in his timing.
Ask God to help you show up for {name} this week, not just pray from a distance.
Name a burden you’ve been carrying by yourself. Ask God to send help, and to help you accept it.
Request a steady heart for the exam, appointment or big meeting coming up.
Pray for the grace to be misunderstood without needing to win the argument.
Ask God for gentleness when you’re tired and running low on patience.
Bring God the situation you can’t fix. Ask him to work where you can’t.
Pray for energy for the next task on your list, and the wisdom to rest when it’s done.
Seek God’s help to tell the truth this week, even where a small lie would be easier.
Ask God for creativity to solve the problem that’s been stuck all week.
Make one bold request today. Tell God exactly what you’re asking for and why.
Pray for peace in a relationship that feels tense right now. Ask God to start with you.
Facing a deadline? Ask God for clear thinking, steady hands and enough time.
Ask God to give you a hunger for him that’s bigger than your hunger for your feed.
Tell God where you feel discouraged. Ask him for hope you can hold onto today.
After a disappointment, ask God to keep your heart from turning bitter.
Name a fear you’ve never said out loud. Ask God for courage bigger than it.
Ask God to make you a good friend this week, the kind you’d want to have.
Ask God for strength to keep going on something you’re tempted to quit.
Lift your mental health to God. Ask him for steady days and good support around you.
Need consistency? Ask God for help showing up for one good habit every day this week.
Tell God about the conflict you’re in. Ask for wisdom to know when to speak and when to stay quiet.
Going somewhere soon? Ask God for safe travels and good company on the way.
Whether this week brings wins or losses, ask God to keep you humble and steady.
Bring God the test result, phone call or news you’re waiting on. Ask him for peace while you wait.
Invite God into the part of your life you’ve been keeping from him. Ask what he’d change.

Ask God to be with you in the next ten minutes.
Say one honest sentence to God. That’s enough.
Thank God for one thing you can see right now.
Ask God to guard your heart while you scroll.
Name one person and ask God to bless them today.

Ask God to help you notice what matters today.
Say “God, I’m here” and mean it.
Ask God for patience with the next person you talk to.
Thank God for something that made you smile today.
Ask God to quiet the noise in your head.
Tell God you trust him with today.
Ask God to help you see people, not just posts.
Thank God for food, water and a place to rest.
Ask God for strength for whatever’s next.
Breathe in: “You are with me.” Breathe out: “I’m not alone.”
Ask God to make you kind, online and off.
Thank God for a friend who gets you.
Ask God to help you put the phone down when it’s time.
Tell God one thing you’re grateful for today.
Ask God to bless your work today.
Pray for someone who’s having a hard day.
Thank God for his patience with you.
Ask God to fill you with joy, not comparison.
Ask God to help you rest well tonight.
Thank God that you don’t have to earn his love.
Ask God to lead your next decision.

Thank God for this breath, and the next one.
Ask God to protect the people you love.
Ask God to help you be fully present with whoever is in front of you.
Thank God for one answered prayer.
Ask God to give you a soft heart today.

Thank God for the quiet of this moment.
Ask God to remind you who you are before the feed tries to.
Tell God, “Your will, not mine, today.”
Ask God to help you choose what’s good, not just what’s easy.
Thank God for the people who pray for you.
Ask God to heal something that’s been hurting.
Ask God to bless someone who annoyed you today.
Thank God for a beautiful thing you saw recently.
Ask God for wisdom in one area of your life.
Tell God you’re sorry for one thing, and let his grace land.
Ask God to help you speak gently today.
Thank God for your home, whatever it looks like right now.
Ask God to calm your anxious thoughts.
Pray for your family in one sentence.
Thank God that today is a fresh start.
Ask God to help you listen more than you talk.
Ask God to show you one way to help someone today.

Tell God one thing you’re hoping for.

Ask God to keep you honest today.
Thank God for one thing your body does well.
Ask God for peace about tomorrow.
Pray for someone who doesn’t know God yet.
Thank God for the season you’re in, even the hard parts.
Ask God to fill the space your phone usually fills.
Tell God, “I want more of you today.”
Ask God to help you be generous today.
Thank God for your favorite part of today so far.
Ask God to bless your city and the people in it.
Ask God to help you stop comparing yourself to anyone online.

Ask God to help you make one good choice in the next hour.
Tell God you’re glad he’s with you.

Ask God to help you love someone well today.
Pray for peace somewhere in the world that’s hurting today.

Ask God to slow you down.
Thank God for every good gift today, including the ones you didn’t notice.
Ask God to bless the next person you message.
Tell God what’s weighing on you, then let him hold it.
Ask God to help you keep your promises.
Thank God for forgiving you.
Ask God to help you see the good in someone.
Pray for a coworker or classmate by name.
Thank God for this chance to pray before you scroll.
Ask God to make you brave today.
Ask God to make you content with what you have.
Thank God for the sky, the trees, the rain or the sun.
Ask God to guide your words in your next conversation.
Pray for someone who’s lonely right now.

family: Walk through your home in your mind, room by room, and pray for whoever sleeps in each one.
Picture your mom or dad right now. Ask God to give them what they need most this week.
Thank God for one thing your parents got right, even if they also got things wrong.
Ask God to be close to the family member you find hardest to love.
Tell God about the argument at home that keeps repeating. Ask him for a new way through it.
Pray for each of your siblings by name, one honest sentence for each.
If you have kids, say each of their names and ask God to protect their hearts today.
Bring your spouse before God. Ask him to help you be a little kinder to them tonight.
Think of a grandparent, living or gone. Thank God for what they passed down to you.
Someone in your family lives far away. Ask God to be near them in the ways you can’t.
Hand God the blended parts of your family: new names, old hurts, and the hope in between.
Ask God for patience with the person at home who knows exactly how to push your buttons.
Tell God which family member you miss most right now. Let yourself feel it for a moment.
Whisper the names of family you’ve lost. Thank God for the years you had with them.
Is there a family relationship that went quiet? Ask God if there’s one small step to take.
Invite God to make your home a place where people can rest, not just pass through.
Pray for the parent who is tired today, whether that’s you or someone you love.
Thank God for a family tradition, even a silly one, that makes you feel at home.
Lift up the kids in your family who are growing up fast. Ask God to keep them close.
Ask God to begin healing an old family wound you don’t usually talk about.
Choose one way to serve your family tonight. Ask God for the energy to follow through.
Is there a sibling you’ve drifted from? Tell God what you wish were different.
Pray for your stepparents, stepkids or in-laws by name. Ask God to grow trust between you.
Ask God to give your parents health, peace and good company as they get older.
Tell God the thing you wish your family understood about you.
Thank God for the person in your family who always picks up the phone.
Give God a family decision that feels too big. Ask for wisdom for everyone involved.
When home feels heavy, say so. Tell God what makes it hard right now.
Cover every person in your family with a short prayer, wherever each of them is right now.
A cousin, aunt or uncle crossed your mind recently. Pray for them now. Maybe that’s why.
Forgive a family member before God, even if you’re still learning to mean it.
Imagine your family around one table. Ask God to be the one holding it together.
Grief changes a family. Ask God to comfort each person who is missing someone.
Tell God about the family you hope to have one day, and trust him with the timing.
Remember a moment this year when your family surprised you with kindness. Thank God for it.
Ask God to break any unhealthy pattern that has been handed down in your family.
Pray for the family member who doesn’t know God yet. Ask him to draw them gently.
Some families are complicated. Tell God about yours exactly as it is, no polish needed.
Listen first. Ask God to help you hear your parents, kids or siblings without rushing to fix.
Say the name of someone at home and ask God to help them feel seen today.
Recall the home you grew up in. Thank God for what was good there, however small.
Bring God any sibling rivalry, old or new. Ask him to turn it into something gentler.
Before the evening gets busy, ask God for peace in your home tonight.
Offer God the family member you worry about most. Leave them in his hands for a minute.
friends: Name the friend you’d call at 2 a.m. Thank God for them and ask him to bless their week.
Ask God which friend needs a check-in today, then send that text.
Tell God honestly how lonely you’ve felt lately. He isn’t put off by it.
Pray for a friend who is struggling right now. Ask God to give them one good day.
Think of a friendship that cooled. Tell God what happened and how it still feels.
Ask God to bring one new friend into your life this season, and to help you notice them.
Thank God for an old friend who still feels like home, no matter how long it’s been.
Is there a friend you owe an apology? Ask God for the humility to say it soon.
Picture your closest friends one by one. Ask God to protect each of them today.
Bring God the friend who seems fine but might not be. Ask him to reach them.
Ask God to make you the kind of friend you wish you had.
Tell God about the group chat that leaves you feeling left out. Ask him for peace about it.
Someone you love moved away. Ask God to surround them with good people where they are.
Hurt by a friend? Tell God what happened and ask him to show you what to do next.
Choose one friend you’ve been taking for granted. Thank God for them, then tell them.
When you feel invisible to your friends, say so to God. He sees you clearly.
Lift up a friend who is waiting on something big. Ask God to steady them in the meantime.
Ask God for courage to go first: the invite, the text, the hello.
Pray for a friend whose faith feels shaky right now. Ask God to stay patient and near.
Think of someone new you met recently. Ask God if this could become a real friendship.
Tell God about the friend you envy a little. Ask him to turn it into real joy for them.
Thank God for friends who told you the truth when it was hard to hear.
Forgive a friend in your heart today, even if they never ask you to.
Pray for the friend going through a breakup, a loss, or a hard family season.
Is there a friendship you need to let go of? Ask God for wisdom and kindness in it.
Hold a friend’s name before God for a few slow breaths. Let that be the whole prayer.
Admit where you’ve been a hard friend to have lately. Ask God to grow you.
Loneliness can feel loud. Ask God to sit with you in it and send someone your way.
Remember a friend who helped you through something hard. Thank God they showed up.
Pray for the friend who always takes care of everyone else. Ask God to take care of them.
Look for the person on the edge of your circle. Ask God how to include them.
Tell God which friendships feel one-sided. Ask him how to love well without burning out.
Whisper the name of a friend you haven’t talked to in ages. Ask God to bless them today.
Thank God for the friend who makes you laugh until you can’t breathe.
Bring God a friend who feels far from him. Ask him to keep pursuing them gently.
Ask God to help you be fully there the next time you’re with friends, phone away.
Pray that your friendships would be honest, kind and good for each other’s souls.
If making friends feels hard right now, tell God. Ask him for one open door.
A friend is sick or worn out. Ask God to give them strength and real rest.
Bless a friend from a season of life that’s over. Ask God to be good to them where they are now.
Ask God to mend a friendship that cracked over something small.
Go through your friends’ names with God, one by one, asking him to be near each.
Celebrate with God for a friend who has good news. Ask him to multiply their joy.
Say thank you to God for the friends you have, even if it’s fewer than you’d like.
healing: Tell God where it hurts, in your body or your heart. Be as specific as you can.
Ask God to be near you in the pain, whatever the next appointment says.
Name the symptom or diagnosis that scares you. Hand it to God, fear and all.
Lament honestly. Tell God this is hard and you wish it were different.
Pray for your doctors, nurses and caregivers. Ask God for wisdom and steady hands.
Someone is sick tonight. Ask God to comfort them and give them rest.
Notice one part of you that isn’t hurting right now. Thank God for that small mercy.
Ask God for strength for the treatment, the waiting room, or the long night ahead.
If you’re tired of asking for healing, tell God that too. He can handle your weariness.
Bring God the emotional wound that never shows up on a scan. Ask him to tend it.
Ask God to heal what he will, and to hold you through whatever stays.
Picture God sitting beside your bed or chair. Tell him what today has been like.
Pray for a friend in recovery. Ask God for courage for each small step they take.
Ask God for patience with a body that won’t move at the pace you want.
Tell God about the memory that still hurts. Ask him to begin mending it gently.
Whisper “I trust you” to God, even if you only partly mean it right now.
Lift up the families caring for someone sick. Ask God to renew their strength.
Name someone in the hospital or waiting on results. Ask God to calm them while they wait.
Chronic pain wears people down. Ask God for relief and for people who understand.
Rest is part of healing. Ask God to let your body sleep well and wake with strength.
Thank God for the people who have shown up for you while you’ve been hurting.
Carrying a mental health struggle quietly? Tell God, and ask him to lead you to people who can help.
Tell God what you’re afraid this illness or injury might take from you. Stay honest with him.
Ask God for hope that isn’t tied to a test result.
Pray for anyone grieving a body that changed through injury, illness or age.
Bring God the relationship that broke and still aches. Ask him to heal what can be healed.
On days when nothing seems to improve, ask God to be your comfort anyway.
Thank God for medicine, therapists, and everyone whose work helps people heal.
Breathe slowly and ask God to bring calm to every part of you that feels tense.
When the pain makes prayer hard, just say “help.” That counts as praying.
Childhood wounds can linger. Ask God to tend yours slowly and kindly.
Is there someone whose healing you stopped praying about? Bring them back to God today.
Frustrated with waiting? Tell God exactly how you feel. Honest prayer is welcome here.
Seek God’s wisdom about your next step in care, and the courage to take it.
Remember a time God carried you through something painful. Thank him for staying.
Lay your hand where it hurts, if you can. Ask God to meet you there.
Pray for sick children and the parents who sit beside their beds.
Say to God, “I don’t understand why this is happening,” and ask him to stay close anyway.
Even on a hard day, look for one small kindness. Thank God for it without pretending the pain is gone.
Hold before God the people who are dying today, and those who love them.
Pray for healing between you and someone you hurt, or who hurt you.
For these few minutes, ask God to give you rest from the fear.
Offer God your body as it is today, tired or strong, and ask him to care for it.
Grief is a wound too. Tell God who or what you’re grieving and let him hold it with you.
anxiety: Breathe in slowly. As you breathe out, tell God the one worry that’s loudest right now.
Name what you’re anxious about in one plain sentence. God isn’t surprised by it.
Put your feet flat on the floor. Ask God to steady you right here, right now.
Tell God the worst-case story your mind keeps telling. Ask him to sit with you in it.
You don’t have to calm down before you pray. Bring God your racing heart as it is.
Ask God for peace in the next five minutes. Just the next five.
Feeling anxious isn’t failing. Tell God how your body feels right now.
Look for three things you can see. Thank God he’s present in this exact room.
Hand God the conversation you’re dreading. Ask him to go ahead of you into it.
If your chest feels tight, slow your breathing and say, “God, I’m here. Stay with me.”
Pick one what-if that keeps looping. Ask God to help you stay in today instead.
Tomorrow’s worry can wait. Tell God about it, then ask him to help you set it down tonight.
Picture placing your worry in God’s open hands. Let him hold it for a while.
Ask God to remind you that reaching out for help, to people or professionals, is a strong thing to do.
Pray for everyone else feeling anxious right now. You’re not the only one.
Say “one thing at a time” to God, and ask him to show you the next one thing.
Anxious days don’t make God love you less. Thank him for loving you exactly the same today.
List what you can control today and what you can’t. Ask God to carry the second list.
Is there something you keep checking, refreshing or rereading? Ask God for rest from that loop.
Whisper, “I am held,” three times slowly. Let each one land a little deeper.
Be gentle with yourself today. Ask God to show you how he is gentle with you.
When panic rises, you can pray in two words: “Help me.” God hears that completely.
Notice where you’re holding tension. Ask God to help you loosen it, one breath at a time.
Underneath this worry, is there a deeper fear? Take your time and tell God what you find.
Is your mind racing about money, school or health? Name it and ask God for clear thinking.
Remember a time you were afraid and got through it. Thank God for walking you through.
Unclench your jaw and drop your shoulders. Then tell God, “Here I am. Stay close.”
If anxiety has felt heavy for a while, ask God for courage to talk to someone who can help.
Pray for sleep that comes easily tonight, and for a mind that can let go of the day.
Find one thing that is okay right now, even if a lot isn’t. Thank God for it.
Admit to God that you’re scared. You don’t have to explain why it shouldn’t bother you.
Imagine God sitting beside you, unhurried. Tell him what’s spinning in your head.
Give God the decision you keep going back and forth on. Ask for peace, not perfection.
Your worth isn’t measured by how calm you feel. Tell God what you need today.
Count four breaths in and four breaths out. Pray “peace” on each exhale.
Nervous about a social situation? Bring it to God and ask him for ease and courage.
Tell God what you’d say if you weren’t trying to sound okay.
Ask God to help you take the next small step instead of solving everything at once.
Hold your worry up to God like a question. Ask him what he wants you to know.
Lift up anyone you love who lives with anxiety. Ask God to comfort them tonight.
Rest your hand on your chest. Thank God for every heartbeat, steady or fast.
Name the thing you’re avoiding because it feels too big. Ask God to help you face one piece.
Let God have the next hour. Ask him to walk through it with you.
God isn’t anxious about your future. Ask him to share some of his calm with you.
work: Name the task you’re dreading most today. Ask God for the focus to start it.
Pray for your boss, teacher or professor by name. Ask God to give them wisdom.
Tell God about the deadline that’s stressing you. Ask him for a clear plan.
Before the exam or presentation, ask God for a calm mind and good recall.
Thank God for your job or your classes, even on the days you’d rather skip them.
Ask God to help you do excellent work on the parts nobody will notice.
Think of a coworker or classmate who seems to be struggling. Pray for them now.
Bring God the email you keep putting off. Ask for the right words and the nerve to send it.
Ask God for wisdom about your career or major, one step at a time.
If work feels pointless right now, tell God. Ask him to show you who it serves.
Pray for the difficult person at work or school. Ask God to help you treat them fairly.
Thank God for one thing you learned this week, in class, at work or by mistake.
Ask God to help you rest without guilt once today’s work is done.
Tell God about the job search: the applications, the silence. Ask him to keep you hopeful.
Lift up your team or study group. Ask God for good teamwork and kind words.
Grades and paychecks invite comparison. Ask God to keep your eyes on your own work.
Pray for students cramming tonight and teachers grading late. Ask God to give them strength.
Look for one way your work can help someone today. Ask God to help you do it well.
Where do you feel behind? Tell God, and ask him to help you take the next small step.
Speaking up is hard. Ask God for courage in the meeting or class discussion.
Thank God for a coworker or classmate who made a hard week easier.
Got bad news at work or school? Tell God exactly how it felt.
Leave work at work tonight. Ask God to help you be present with the people at home.
Bring God the group project, the shift, or the meeting you’re dreading.
Pray for wisdom with your time today: what to start, what to drop, and when to stop.
Ask God to make you a calm presence in a stressful workplace or classroom.
Share with God what you hope your work will mean someday. Trust him with the timing.
Remember anyone who lost a job or is struggling in school. Ask God to provide for them.
Feedback can sting. Ask God to help you take it without falling apart or getting defensive.
Whisper a prayer over your to-do list. Ask God to help you choose what matters most.
Is a shortcut tempting you at work or school? Ask God for integrity instead.
Choose one assignment or task for the next hour. Ask God to help you give it your full attention.
Tell God about the burnout you’ve been pushing through. Ask him for real rest.
Celebrate a coworker’s or classmate’s win with God, and ask him to clear away any envy.
Before you study, ask God to help you understand, not just memorize.
Picture the people who make your work possible. Ask God to bless them today.
Offer your work to God today as worship, not just something to get through.
Customers, clients or classmates testing you? Ask God for patience with them today.
A decision about your future feels too big. Ask God for peace while you decide.
Interview, test or review coming up? Ask God to keep you calm and clear.
Imagine walking into work or class with God beside you. Ask him to come along today.
Your worth doesn’t depend on your grades or your title. Thank God for that today.
Ask God to show you one person at work or school who needs encouragement.
Commit today’s work to God. Ask him to make it useful to someone.
gratitude: Notice one thing today that went right without your help. Thank God for it by name.
List five gifts from the last 24 hours, slowly. Let each one be its own small thank you.
Picture someone who loves you. Tell God what you’re grateful for in them.
Remember where you were a year ago. Name one thing that’s better now, and give God the credit.
Gratitude looks forward too. Name something you’re excited about and thank God for the hope.
Recall a time you were lost, in life or on a map, and someone pointed the way. Thank God for them.
Your phone keeps showing you what you lack. For one minute, tell God what you already have.
Choose one person you rarely thank. Thank God for them, then think of a way to thank them too.
Count the people who helped you this week, even in small ways. Thank God for each one.
Tell God about a good surprise from this week, and thank him for the timing.
Bring to mind the simplest pleasure you enjoyed today. Say, “Thank you, that was from you.”
Write a mental thank-you note to God for one thing about your life right now.
Look at your hands. Thank God for the work, the hugs and the meals they’ve made possible.
Instead of rushing on, linger over one good thing from today and tell God why it mattered.
Name a sound you love, like rain or someone’s laugh. Thank God for ears to hear it.
Think about the language you speak. Thank God that you can talk to him in your own words.
Start small: thank God for the floor under your feet and the light you’re reading by.
Say thank you to God for three good things you didn’t have to pay for today.
Recall a time someone stood up for you. Thank God for their courage.
Name one thing about where you live that you’d miss if you moved. Thank God for it today.
Think of a prayer that’s still unanswered. Thank God for staying with you while you wait.
Be thankful for someone who disagrees with you but still treats you kindly. Tell God about them.
Picture the last person who smiled at you. Thank God for that small moment of warmth.
Remember who first taught you about God. Thank him for that person by name.
Thank God for the gift of imagination. Tell him about one dream you’re carrying.
When did you feel at home this week? Thank God for that moment and who was there.
Ask God to help you see your life with grateful eyes. Then name the first good thing you notice.
Swap one complaint for a thank you. Name the complaint, then find the gift hiding inside it.
Who makes you laugh the most? Thank God for them, and ask him to bless their day.
Notice your heartbeat for a moment. Thank God that it keeps going without you asking.
Pause and name a gift you have that someone else is praying for today. Thank God for it.
Remember your first home or bedroom. Thank God for every place that has sheltered you.
Pick a comfort you’d only notice if it broke, like heat or Wi-Fi. Thank God that it works today.
Tell God one thing you’ll miss about this stage of life when it’s over.
Thank God for the people you’ll see today, before you even see them.
Whisper “thank you” to God three times, thinking of a different gift each time.
Find a habit in your life that’s good for you. Thank God for the strength to keep it.
Thank God for a problem you don’t have. Name it, and let that sink in.
Imagine losing your phone for a week. Name what you’d still have, and thank God for it.
Celebrate someone else’s good news with God. Thank him for what he’s doing in their life.
Turn your attention to what’s right in front of you. Thank God for this hour, as it is.
Choose one word for how this year has gone. Thank God for one good thing inside that word.
Name a friend you haven’t talked to in a while. Thank God for what they brought into your life.
Before you open anything else, tell God one reason today is worth thanking him for.
forgiveness: Name the thing you’re most afraid God won’t forgive. Say it plainly, then rest in his mercy.
Ask God to help you receive his forgiveness instead of trying to earn it.
Is someone’s name making your chest tight? Tell God what they did, and how much it hurt.
Forgiving isn’t pretending it didn’t hurt. Tell God the truth about the wound first.
You can forgive someone and still keep your distance. Ask God for wisdom and peace in both.
Picture handing God a heavy bag with someone’s name on it. Ask him to hold it for you today.
Tell God you’re not ready to forgive yet, if that’s true. Ask him to stay with you there.
Thank God that his forgiveness doesn’t run out, even for the same mistake twice.
Bring God a regret from years ago that still stings. Ask him to help you stop carrying it.
Forgive yourself for one thing God already forgave. Say, “If he let it go, I can too.”
Pray one small blessing over someone who hurt you. It’s okay if you only half mean it today.
Ask God to help you stop rehearsing what you’d say to someone who hurt you.
Name the apology you never got. Tell God how that feels, and ask him to meet you there.
If shame has been talking louder than grace, tell God what it keeps saying. Then listen for his reply.
Say to God, “I want to be free of this resentment, even if I don’t know how yet.”
Ask God to heal the part of you that still flinches when you think of what happened.
Forgiveness can start as a choice before it’s a feeling. Tell God if you’re ready to choose it.
Imagine God looking at your worst moment with kindness, not disgust. Stay there for a breath.
Is it hard to accept forgiveness from someone who already forgave you? Tell God why.
Release one small offense from this week, a comment or a slight. Tell God you’re letting it go.
Lay down the scorecard you keep on someone. Ask God to help you stop counting.
Hold out your open hands and picture God placing forgiveness in them. Say thank you.
Grace can feel too good to be true. Tell God what makes it hard for you to believe.
Pray for the person you need to apologize to. Ask God for humble words and good timing.
Some wounds come from church or people of faith. Tell God about yours honestly.
Tell God about the version of you that you’re still embarrassed by. He isn’t embarrassed by you.
Remember a time you were truly sorry. Thank God for how he met you then.
Let God have the last word on what happened. Tell him the part you still can’t make sense of.
Talk to God about someone who hurt you online. Ask him to help you stop checking on them.
You are more than your worst mistake. Tell God the label you’ve stuck on yourself and ask him to remove it.
Picture yourself the way God sees you after he forgives: clean, loved, welcome. Thank him.
Admit any bitterness you’ve been calling “being right.” Ask God to loosen its grip.
Ask God what forgiveness could look like here: one small step, not the whole road.
Name one person you’ve already forgiven. Thank God for the freedom that came with it.
Bring God the mistake you made today. Hear him say, “You’re still mine.”
When anger flares today, breathe and say, “God, I give this to you again.”
Forgiving a parent can be the hardest kind. Tell God honestly where you are with yours.
Hand God the guilt you’ve already confessed. You don’t have to keep picking it back up.
Pray for patience with the small things: the late reply, the rude driver, the snide comment.
Thank God for someone who showed you what forgiveness looks like by how they lived.
If you’re angry at God about something, tell him honestly. He can handle your hurt.
If you hurt someone and they won’t forgive you, tell God. Ask for peace with what you can’t fix.
Ask God to show you how much you’ve been forgiven, so you can be gentle with others.
Sit quietly and receive this: you are forgiven. Breathe it in before you breathe out.
guidance: Name the decision you keep circling. Tell God what scares you about each option.
Waiting is hard. Tell God how long it’s felt, and ask him for patience just for today.
Two good options can be harder than one bad one. Ask God for wisdom to choose well.
Bring your college or school choice to God. Ask him to guide you past fear and pressure.
Tell God what you’d try if you weren’t afraid of failing. Ask him if it’s worth exploring.
Think of someone wise you trust. Ask God whether to talk this decision over with them.
Hold your plans loosely for a minute. Tell God you’re open to a better idea than yours.
Ask God to show you what you’re missing about this choice: a risk, a gift or a person.
Pray about your career: not just what pays, but what kind of person the work will make you.
Lay out your options before God one by one. Notice which one brings peace as you pray.
If you’re in a relationship, ask God for clarity about where it’s headed and honesty to face it.
Single and wondering? Tell God what you hope for, and ask him to guide your heart while you wait.
Whose opinion is loudest in your decision? Ask God to help you weigh it against his.
Thank God for guiding you before. Name a time a choice only made sense later.
Say to God, “I don’t know what to do.” Then ask him to lead you anyway.
Picture yourself a year from now. Ask God which choice today you’d be glad you made.
Ask God to slow you down if you’re rushing a decision out of fear.
Pray over the application, interview or email you’re about to send. Leave the outcome with God.
Is a gut feeling nagging at you about something? Ask God whether it’s a warning or just nerves.
Tell God what success looks like to you. Ask if it matches what he cares about.
Wondering about your major or your next job? Ask God to show you what makes you come alive.
Ask God for courage to say no to a good thing so you can say yes to the right one.
Name one relationship that’s changing. Ask God how to hold it with love and wisdom.
Feel behind your friends? Tell God where, and ask him to help you trust his timing for you.
Pray for the people your decision will affect. Ask God to help you consider them well.
Hand God the timeline you’ve been clinging to. Ask him for trust while you wait.
When the right choice is also the hard one, tell God honestly what it will cost you.
Think about your gifts. Ask God where he might want you to use them this year.
Tell God about the door that closed. Ask him what you can learn while you look for the next.
Ask God to guard you from choosing something just to impress people.
Moving, transferring or staying put? Bring every pro and con to God and talk it through.
Write the question you’re asking God in one sentence. Pray it slowly, then listen.
Be honest: is there an answer you already know but don’t like? Tell God.
Pray for wisdom about a friendship that’s been draining you. Ask God what healthy looks like.
Ask God to help you finish what you started before you jump to something new.
Listen for a minute without asking anything. Notice what comes to mind and bring it to God.
Dating someone or hoping to? Ask God for wisdom that goes deeper than feelings.
Check your motives with God. Tell him honestly why you want this choice.
Feeling stuck? Ask God to show you one small thing you can do today.
Offer God your fear of choosing wrong. Ask him to lead you even through a misstep.
Trust doesn’t mean having every answer. Tell God you’ll take the next step with him.
Thank God that you don’t have to figure out your whole life today.
Imagine explaining your choice to someone who loves you. Ask God if it still feels right.
Look at what’s in front of you today. Ask God to help you be faithful there while the big answer waits.
morning: Before your feet hit the floor, tell God, “This day is yours. Lead me through it.”
Name the first thing on today’s schedule. Invite God into it before it starts.
Good morning, God. Tell him one thing you’re looking forward to and one you’re dreading.
Ask God to set the tone for today before your notifications do.
Thank God for last night’s sleep, even if it was short, and ask him for energy for today.
Picture walking through your day: each meeting, class or task. Ask God to go ahead of you.
Pick one word for how you want to live today, like patient or brave. Ask God for it.
Open your hands and say, “Today I receive what you give and release what I can’t control.”
Pray for whoever will make your coffee, drive your bus or teach your class today.
Tell God how you actually woke up feeling. Start there, not where you think you should be.
Ask God for one chance today to be kind to someone who doesn’t expect it.
It’s a new day. Hand God anything left over from yesterday.
Breathe deep before the rush. Tell God which part of today you most want him in.
Commit your to-do list to God. Ask him which item matters most.
Ask God to help you notice him at least once before tonight.
Before you check the news or your feed, tell God one thing you trust him with today.
Pray for the people you’ll work or study with today, by name if you can.
Say, “God, give me enough strength for today, not the whole week.” Then breathe.
Think of someone at school or work who seems lonely. Ask God for a way to include them today.
Make your first sip of the day a prayer. Tell God one thing you need from him today.
Ask God to catch you before you snap at someone today, and give you a deep breath instead.
Morning is a fresh page. Ask God what he wants written on it today.
Pray that your phone would serve your day today, not steal it.
Tell God which task you’ve been putting off. Ask him for the push to start it first.
Invite God into the parts of today you’re least excited about.
Choose one thing you’ll do today just because it’s good. Ask God to bless it.
Stretch, then pray: “Thank you for this body. Help me use it well today.”
Let your first words today be to God, not to a screen. Tell him what you hope for.
Give God your calendar. Ask him to make room for the unplanned moments he might bring.
Get ready for the day with God: as you get dressed, ask him to clothe you with patience.
Pray for your family as they start their day, wherever they are.
Name one gift waiting for you today: a person, a meal, a moment. Thank God ahead of time.
Ask God to guide the first choice you make today, even a small one like your tone.
Whether it’s light outside yet or not, thank God for a day you didn’t have to earn.
Set one intention with God: one person to encourage, one task to finish well.
Today will have surprises. Ask God for flexibility and a calm heart when plans change.
Tell God you’re available. Ask him to use you somewhere unexpected today.
Bless your day out loud: “God, bless my work, my words and my people today.”
If you woke up anxious, name the reason to God. Ask him to walk into it with you.
Thank God for one thing you get to do today that you genuinely enjoy.
Plan one moment later today to pause and pray again. Ask God to remind you.
Picture yourself at the end of today, at peace. Ask God what would help you get there.
